title: Farmer's Breakfast Casserole
subtitle: Hash browns, sausage, eggs, and cheese baked in one deep dish.
description: Adapted from classic Midwest farm-kitchen breakfast bake tradition for firehall oven service: shredded hash browns layered with browned breakfast sausage, eggs, milk, and cheddar baked until puffed and golden for ten portions.

ingredients.name: sliced green onions
ingredients.notes: plus hot sauce at the line

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Farmer's Breakfast Casserole in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a deep 9x13 pan or hotel half-pan. Thaw hash browns completely and squeeze out excess water in a clean towel—wet potatoes make a soggy casserole. Allow 10–15 minutes for mise en place before heat goes on. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.instruction: Cook breakfast sausage in a skillet over medium-high, breaking into small crumbles until no pink remains and internal temperature reaches 160°F. Drain on paper towels. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Layer the base
steps.instruction: Spread hash browns evenly in the pan. Top with sausage and half the cheddar. Whisk eggs, milk, mustard, salt, and pepper until uniform and pour evenly over the layers. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bake until set
steps.instruction: Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes. Uncover, top with remaining cheddar, and bake 15 more until center reaches 165°F on a thermometer and top is golden. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest casserole 10 minutes before cutting so slices hold clean squares. Garnish with green onions and serve with hot sauce at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Squeeze hash browns dry—this is the single biggest factor in a crisp versus soggy base.
Cover for the first half of baking so top cheese does not over-brown before center sets.
Cut with a sharp bench scraper in the pan for even ten-portion squares.
cleanupNotes: Soak the 9x13 with hot water while still warm before baked egg residue sets.
Drain sausage grease into a heat-safe container, never down the sink.
leftovers: Reheat portions covered at 325°F for 12 minutes until steaming in the center.
Cube leftovers into breakfast burrito filling with salsa and extra cheese.
